To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a weight-control program with a moderate intensity physical activity component is effective in decreasing fat mass and increasing lipid oxidation rate and VO2max in obese children.

an 8-month multi-disciplinary weight-control programme, including 2 hours of moderate-intensity physical activity, nutritional and psychological education, induces a significant decrease in body mass index and body fat mass, an increase in lipid oxidation rate during physical exercise and in time devoted to recreational physical activity in free-living condition in obese children.

a multidisciplinary weight-loss program with moderate-intensity activities induces a decrease in body mass index, a reduction of fat mass, an increase of maximal oxygen uptake and an increase in the lipid oxidation rate during the exercise in obese children.

the effects of weight-control program, based on moderate-intensity physical activity, on body composition, energy expenditure, and lipid oxidation rate in obese children.
the effects of a weight control program on the body composition and lipid metabolism of obese children.
the effects of a weight-control program on lipid oxidation during exercise in obese school-aged children.

a multidisciplinary weight control program, with moderate intensity physical activities, induced decrease in fat mass, increase in maximal oxygen uptake, lipid oxidation rate and time spent on recreational activities.

the multidisciplinary approach to weight loss in obese children is effective in improving body composition and physical fitness.
the multidisciplinary weight-loss program was effective in reducing body weight, body fat, and increasing VO2max in obese children.
